<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**8** anchor(s) derived from **2** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/src/shared/protocol-upgrade-guide.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/src/shared/protocol-upgrade-guide.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **176** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2513e3ad90dbba61b05230693a713465c7828950` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `199023efc06822473fdec75e1ee26bb4f9c106a9` — the merge of head `c10c6e1a172dab79c577dd7eafc9cdeb453ee26d` into base `2513e3ad90dbba61b05230693a713465c7828950`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 199023efc06822473fdec75e1ee26bb4f9c106a9 && git checkout 199023efc06822473fdec75e1ee26bb4f9c106a9
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 2513e3ad90dbba61b05230693a713465c7828950 c10c6e1a172dab79c577dd7eafc9cdeb453ee26d && git checkout -B drift-repro 2513e3ad90dbba61b05230693a713465c7828950 && git merge --no-ff c10c6e1a172dab79c577dd7eafc9cdeb453ee26d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2513e3ad90dbba61b05230693a713465c7828950
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `38757206af028eb1ba0fb3b56bdd1a743c8a0907`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/shared/suggestions.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/shared/protocol-upgrade-guide.ts + packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts

### ① Derived judgments

- New optional `retiredKeyUpgradeGuide?: boolean` on the exported `StrictUnknownKeyErrorOptions`: right. It is additive and type-only; no runtime accept set moves.
- Default `true` (destructured): right. The default branch is byte-identical to `main`.
- Metadata surfaces keep the sentence: right. The only in-spec caller, `strictObjectError` (`strict-object.ts:347`), does not pass the member, and `StrictObjectOptions` cannot forward it. The console's own aged-out refusal builds its sentence independently.
- api-surface report not regenerated: right. `api-surface/shared.json` records names and kinds only, and the function signature is unchanged.
- MCP refusal text: the 17 `strictToolInput` tools lose the sentence. That is right as code, but the description is wrong; see ④ S1.
- `recordId` descriptions: right. Text only, on exactly the six takers; no argument, alias or answer shape moves.
- Gates: every check-run on the head is `success` or `skipped`.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/spec` patch and `@objectstack/mcp` patch match what the diff publishes, given `Metadata-protocol: none`. `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` appear in the body and in both changesets, and agree with seat ruling 6807273553. Nit: the spec changeset title is `feat(spec)` at patch.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty.
- The dev's three deviations are benign: a no-conflict merge of main, a dogfood run that was not owed, and a skipped MCP assignee write that the order forbade.
- Both out-of-scope notes were correctly left alone.
- Escalated to the seat: the dataset tool pair (④ S1).

### ④ Design judgment

- `suggestions.zod.ts`: holds against #25767 D2 = A and the ADR-0087 addendum of 2026-10-26. The opt-out is reachable only through a direct caller of the published factory, and the #5955 sentence order is kept.
  - Nit N1: the docblock still says the factory stays "unchanged" for external callers; it is now additively changed.
  - Nit N2: `!retiredKeyUpgradeGuide` also opts out an untyped `null`/`0`.
- `protocol-upgrade-guide.ts` (docblock only) and `mcp-http-tools.ts`:
  - **S1, should-fix: "every MCP tool" is false for `list_datasets` and `query_dataset`.** These two are registered in the same file with spec `strictObject` input schemas (`dataset-tools.zod.ts:57`, `:202`), not with `strictToolInput`. Their unknown-key refusal still carries the upgrade-guide sentence (by reading). The new sweep test's stub bridge never registers the pair. Keeping the sentence on them is defensible, because those inputs are published spec schemas that can carry a kit. The fix is wording: scope the mcp changeset and the new docblock to the tools that `strictToolInput` closes, and name the pair as keeping the spec refusal. The card's three measured refusals are fixed, and no accept set is wrong, so this is not a must-fix.
  - `recordId` under option (c): holds against #17568 (5630933337). There is no alias and no rename, and the descriptions sit on exactly `get_record`, `update_record`, `delete_record`, `run_action`, `read_file` and `create_upload_link`.
  - Nit N3: "each query_records row carries" the `id`; a `fields` projection may drop it, so "carries by default" would be exact.

A delta review is owed for the S1 fix. Nits N1–N3 are optional.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`

Scope: packages/spec/src/shared/suggestions.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/shared/protocol-upgrade-guide.ts + packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts

### Delta

This record covers the delta from `38757206af028eb1ba0fb3b56bdd1a743c8a0907` (record 6809454807: PASS with should-fix S1). One commit, no merge of `main`, 7 files, +41/-14. Everything not named here stands as judged there. When this was read, the check-runs on this head were still running (none failed); the seat confirms them before landing.

### ① Derived judgments

- The guard changed from `!retiredKeyUpgradeGuide` to `=== false`. This is right and moves no accept set. Typed callers (`true`/`false`/omitted) get identical output. An untyped `null`/`0`/`''` now keeps the sentence, which is the documented default's direction. Only refusal text changes, never which keys are refused.
- Default path: unchanged. `strictObject` still passes no member.
- api-surface: unchanged, rightly.
- `RECORD_ID_DESCRIPTION` "carries by default": right; description only.

### ② Semver level

Both changesets stay patch, with `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` unchanged. The spec changeset title moved from `feat(spec)` to `fix(spec)`, which closes the earlier nit.

### ③ Boundary flags

The dataset tool pair escalated earlier is answered in the tree: it is named as keeping the spec refusal, and pinned. The delta raises no new flag.

### ④ Design judgment

- **S1: resolved.** The mcp changeset ("every tool whose arguments `strictToolInput` closes (all but two)", naming `list_datasets`/`query_dataset`), the `protocol-upgrade-guide.ts` docblock, and the `strictToolInput` comment now agree with the tree. The tree has 19 registrations: 17 through `strictToolInput` and 2 through spec schemas. The CONTROL pin in `mcp-dataset-tools.test.ts` asserts that `list_datasets` with an undeclared top-level key is refused with `-32602`, names the key, contains `RETIRED_KEY_UPGRADE_GUIDE_SENTENCE`, and does not call the bridge.
- **N1, N2, N3: closed.**
- One new nit: the PR body's "What changes" paragraph opened with "Every MCP tool closes its arguments with `strictToolInput`". It is prose only, and the seat corrects it in the body.

No must-fix and no should-fix remain.

Seat record: ACCEPT #32476 · 2026-11-11T23:48Z · head `c10c6e1a172dab79c577dd7eafc9cdeb453ee26d`

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：MCP 工具调用传了未声明的参数时，拒绝信息仍然点名错键并给出正确拼写（`id` → `recordId`、`filter` → `where`），但不再附带「已退役的键请看协议升级指南」那句；六个接收 `recordId` 的工具在参数说明里写明，它就是 `create_record` 回答里、`query_records` 每行默认带的 `id`。数据集两个工具（`list_datasets`、`query_dataset`）的输入是 spec 的发布 schema，保留原拒绝文字。
- 为什么改：MCP 工具参数不是协议元数据，从来没有键退役过，那句话会把 agent 引到一个与它的错误无关的页面；create → update → get 链式调用时，agent 只能靠一次被拒才知道 `id` 要改成 `recordId`。
- 风险与回滚：不改任何参数名、不加别名、不改回答形状（`recordId` 改名与 `id` 别名已在 #17568 被裁拒）。spec 侧只给 `strictUnknownKeyError` 加一个可选开关，默认不变，元数据面的拒绝文字一字不动；回滚即还原本 PR。
- 先看：`packages/spec/src/shared/suggestions.zod.ts` 的 `retiredKeyUpgradeGuide`；`packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts` 的 `strictToolInput` 和 `RECORD_ID_DESCRIPTION`。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/mcp exec vitest run src/mcp-http-tools.unknown-argument-keys.test.ts src/mcp-dataset-tools.test.ts`，预期全过。
- 需要你做的：无，席位按 Tier S 落地；若本会话的落地动作仍被自动模式拦下，请像前四个一样手动转 ready 入队。

席位意见：ACCEPT。拼写问题按 (c) 处理，与 #17568 的裁决一致；拒绝文字只对 `strictToolInput` 收口的 17 个工具关掉那句话。契约档复核 PASS，其中的 should-fix（数据集两工具的表述）已在 delta 复核里确认解决。

## 席位核对

1. Shape: draft PR to `main`. `Fixes #32436` is its only closing keyword, and it sits next to no other open card. 8 files, all within the claim surface as amended in 6807273553: spec `suggestions.zod.ts`, the `protocol-upgrade-guide.ts` docblock and tests, mcp `mcp-http-tools.ts` and two test files, and two patch changesets (`@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/mcp`, both `private: false`). I read both changesets against the diff, including the S1 scoping sentence that names the dataset pair, and they match. I patched the body twice (issue_patch, signed) to correct its "every MCP tool" prose.
2. Premise measured: the step-0 report (`/mnt/project-files/server-seat3-p2/card-32436/step0.md`, on `14754c70`) and the card's three refusals are pinned: `update_record` sent `id`, `query_records` sent `filter`, `list_objects` sent `includeSystem`. Each is refused with `-32602` and no URL. A CONTROL pins that `list_datasets` keeps the sentence. One ablation (the switch back to `true`) turned 4 tests red and left 15 green.
3. Gates on head `c10c6e1a`: every check-run is `success` or an expected skip (60 success, 15 skipped, 0 other), including Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check and Test Core. `mergeable_state` is `clean`; K = 5.
4. Accepted deviations: the api-surface report was not regenerated, which is right because it records names and kinds only. `dual-build-cjs-loads` and `lean-entry-closure` were NOT MEASURED locally (exit 3, prerequisite); CI is green. Contract review: CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER PASS on `38757206` (6809454807, should-fix S1) and a delta PASS on this head (6809686855, S1 resolved).
5. Out of scope: `agent_prompt`'s `recordId` (a prompt argument, not a tool) and the `skill-md.ts` prose, both noted by the dev and left alone. Skills-docs: none (Metadata-protocol: none).
6. Landing: NOT governed, 250 lines ≤ 3000, Tier S. Landing follows `pm:awaiting-merge` as for the four PRs before it, while the seat session's auto-mode refusal of `label-write --land` stands.
